insights.claim: TrustyAI supports two distinct inference payload ingestion mechanisms — a synchronous REST consumer for ModelMesh and an asynchronous Knative CloudEvent consumer for KServe — each with its own reconciler, creating a dual-path data pipeline that must be maintained in parallel.
insights.reasoning: The ConsumerEndpoint at /consumer/kserve/v2 uses ModelMeshInferencePayloadReconciler while CloudEventConsumer uses KServeInferencePayloadReconciler. Both paths reconcile input/output pairs but through different transport mechanisms and reconcilers, which means changes to inference schema or storage must be coordinated across both paths.

insights.claim: The TrustyAI service exposes its full API surface (including data ingestion and metrics computation) without application-level authentication, relying entirely on platform-level enforcement by OpenShift Routes or Service Mesh.
insights.reasoning: The Route explicitly sets tls: null and no application-level auth mechanism (Quarkus Security, OIDC, etc.) is configured in application.properties. If deployed outside a Service Mesh or without Route-level auth, the inference consumer endpoint and metrics API are accessible without authentication.

insights.claim: The RHOAI distribution disables all explainer endpoints (SHAP, LIME, counterfactual, time-series saliency, global) via Quarkus profile-based feature flags, reducing the API surface compared to ODH while sharing the same codebase.
insights.reasoning: The %rhoai profile disables explainer endpoints while %odh enables them all. This means RHOAI and ODH have different API surfaces from the same binary, which affects documentation, testing, and support scope. The feature flag mechanism uses Quarkus configuration profiles rather than build-time exclusion.
